LESSON: WRITING 8.5.1 ASSESSING WRITING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.5: Writing 8.5.1 Assessing Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 8.5.1 Assessing Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are the qualities of a good composition?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the qualities of a well written composition
2. write a composition related to the theme
3. value the need for clarity and cohesion in written communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 8.5.1 ASSESSING WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 8.5.1 Assessing Writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 8.5.1 ASSESSING WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the qualities of a well written composition

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the qualities of a well written composition. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the qualities of a well written composition.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.5.1 Assessing Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the qualities of a well written composition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a composition related to the theme

What this means
In this part you learn to write a composition related to the theme. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a composition related to the theme.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.5.1 Assessing Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a composition related to the theme. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Value the need for clarity and cohesion in written communication

What this means
In this part you learn to value the need for clarity and cohesion in written communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the need for clarity and cohesion in written communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the need for clarity and cohesion in written communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 8.5.1 Assessing Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.5.1 Assessing Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the qualities of a well written composition)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.5.1 Assessing Writing to a partner. (skill: write a composition related to the theme)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: value the need for clarity and cohesion in written communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 8.5.1 Assessing Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the qualities of a well written composition.
3. Practise this skill: write a composition related to the theme.
4. Practise this skill: value the need for clarity and cohesion in written communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 8.5.1 Assessing Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 8.5.1 Assessing Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Writing 8.5.1 Assessing Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the qualities of a good composition?
2. How can one make a composition interesting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 8.5.1 Assessing Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the qualities of a well written composition.
5. Be able to: write a composition related to the theme.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
